articles.body: Most older Gamma walkthroughs still repeat outdated heuristics ( "40 credits per deck" or "Plus includes unlimited AI" ). Under Gamma’s current dynamic billing model, new free accounts receive a one-time pool of 400 credits (no monthly reset)—and how fast those credits burn depends heavily on which generator UI you click and what hidden defaults sit inside the image editor. To measure exact unit economics instead of guessing, I ran a standardized B2B manufacturing website proposal prompt across Gamma’s Classic Generator , Home Agent ( Lite ) , and micro-edit controls —logging every balance delta from 400 down to 309 credits ( 91 spent total) —and then inspected the free .pptx and .pdf exports programmatically with python-pptx , pypdf , and zipfile .

articles.body: A layoff tends to arrive with two urges at once: freeze, or apply to everything immediately. Neither works well. The first week is better spent building a base you can search from: your paperwork in order, your wins written down, your resume updated and a few real conversations started. This plan breaks that into one focus per day. Each day is meant to take a few hours, not a full workday. Leave room to be a person. Day 1: Stabilise Before anything about jobs, handle what has a deadline. Write down your last working day, your severance terms and the end dates of any benefits. Note anything you need to decide by a specific date, and put those dates in a calendar.

articles.body: We check our public parcel tracking page from outside our own network with Prometheus and the blackbox exporter. The exporter runs on a small virtual machine with another cloud provider. Prometheus scrapes its /probe endpoint with the tracking page's URL as a parameter, the exporter requests the page, and it returns the result as metrics. When we set it up, the alert was copied from our node alerts: up{job="blackbox-tracking"} == 0 for two minutes. On a Sunday at the start of November a change to the CDN's origin settings left the tracking page answering 503 for fifty one minutes. Nobody was paged. We heard about it on Monday from customer service, who had spent Sunday evening answering emails about parcels that could not be found. up does not describe the target.

You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is new. The catch is that great books rarely reveal their most fascinating tricks on the first pass. articles.body: The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon)..

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet.

articles.title: 1Password breach leaked customer names and emails, but not passwords
articles.excerpt: 1Password says a hacker stole customer names and email addresses after gaining access to its backend systems. The breach didn't expose passwords or other information stored in customer vaults, but cou…
articles.body: 1Password says a hacker stole customer names and email addresses after gaining access to its backend systems. The breach didn't expose passwords or other information stored in customer vaults, but could put users at risk of phishing attempts, according to a post disclosing the incident . It's unclear how many users are affected. The password manager began investigating the incident on November 19th, after an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account. Using the compromised account, the hacker accessed 1Password's source code and pushed malicious code to backend services to download customer data.
